Given some function f : Fin n → M into a possibly non-commutative monoid M and two i j : Fin n, what's the recommended way to take the product f i * ... * f j (or 1 if j < i)? This seems really basic, but I can't figure it out :sweat_smile:
If the monoid was commutative this would simply be ∏ k ∈ .Icc i j, f k, but that notation uses docs#Finset.prod which in this generality does not apply. I know there's also docs#List.prod for taking the product over a List of elements of a noncommutative monoid, and docs#List.ofFn to create a list from the function f : Fin n → M - but how do I best restrict that to the subinterval I want? I know I could compose f with some function Fin (n - i - j) → Fin n before passing it to List.ofFn, but that seems somewhat unnatural and also involves subtraction of natural numbers - is there a better way?

In case this is an xy problem: I'm currently trying to write down a concrete definition of the nerve of a topological monoid as a simplicial topological space. I know that one can carry this out more generally by constructing the nerve of a monoid object in a cartesian monoidal (maybe even just monoidal?) category as a simplicial object, but that runs into its own problems with how to talk about products of sublists of lists in that setting
Silly, but (Finset.Icc i j).sort |>.map f |>.prod or similar?
heh. that would work for at least quickly defining it, yes
I imagine the .sort won't be particularly nice to work with for proving lemmas, but if nothing else comes up I'll give it a try

How about

import Mathlib
variable {M : Type*} [Monoid M] {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin n) (f : Fin n → M)
#check (i...=j).toList.map f |>.prod

Ben Eltschig said:

In case this is an xy problem: I'm currently trying to write down a concrete definition of the nerve of a topological monoid as a simplicial topological space. I know that one can carry this out more generally by constructing the nerve of a monoid object in a cartesian monoidal (maybe even just monoidal?) category as a simplicial object, but that runs into its own problems with how to talk about products of sublists of lists in that setting

About that part: you can indeed do that for even a monoidal category and it has been kind of an obsession of mine to try and formalize that. I now have a (I think) rather precise plan on how that could be achieved within Mathlib, but I'm a bit swamped by other projects right now for actually implementing it

Roughly speaking, the plan would be to use ideas similar to what I did in the symmetric case here: using coherence theorems, you should be able to view monoidal categories as some kind "pseudo-simplicial categories" (i.e. pseudofunctors from the opposite of the simplex category to Cat), and lax monoidal functor as lax monoidal transformations between such pseudo-simplicial categories. Now, monoid objects in C interpret as lax monoidal functors from the unit monoidal category to C and the lax natural transformation attached to this should encore all the simplicial data you need to package a monoid as a simplicial object like this.
